subject: general
question: Why do epithelial tissues have very little space between their cells?

options.text: To create an effective barrier regulating permeability of substances
To enable them to transmit electrical signals

solution:
The correct answer is __**To create an effective barrier regulating permeability of substances**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Epithelial tissues** are the **covering** or **protective tissues** in the animal body. They cover most organs and cavities within the body.
 
• The cells of epithelial tissue are **tightly packed** and form a **continuous sheet**. This structural arrangement ensures that there is almost **no intercellular space** between the cells.
 
• The primary reason for this tight packing is to act as a **selective barrier**. Since it forms the outermost layer of the body and lines internal organs, any substance entering or leaving the body must cross at least one layer of epithelium.
 
• The **permeability** of these epithelial cells is vital for **regulating the exchange of materials** between the body and the external environment, and between different internal compartments. ***Hence, the statement in option 1 is correct.***
